title: Design System: horsie

chassis.purpose: The recessed column you navigate from: the session rail and the settings nav.

panel.purpose: The surface you read: the content column, and anything that genuinely floats above it.

panel-raised.purpose: Hover, selection, a menu. The one token whose brightness FLIPS between exposures — lighter in the dark, darker in the light — because what it must do is separate from the ground it lands on.

screen.purpose: Tool results, code blocks, log tails, and the fill inside a field. A tint that says 'not written by a person'.

rule.purpose: Reserved for the few lines that carry meaning alone: a tree rail, a graph edge, a horizontal rule. Never for bounding a region.

rule-strong.purpose: The heavier of the two meaningful lines; also the scrollbar thumb.

legend-dim.purpose: Secondary text: descriptions, subtitles, inactive nav.

legend-faint.purpose: Labels and metadata. The tightest AA case in the system.

keycap.purpose: A filled rectangle with no border, so the fill is the only thing separating it from its surface.

accent.purpose: The action that commits, and nothing else.

accent-ink.purpose: Also the focus ring drawn INSIDE the commit key.

accent-quiet.purpose: The SELECTED fill — a row, a nav item, a picked option. Distinct from panel-raised, which is hover: two greys a few points apart cannot say 'pointing at' and 'picked' at once.

live.purpose: A measured value in flight — emissive form, for lamps and meters.

live-ink.purpose: The text form; darkens in light to clear AA.

live-quiet.purpose: Behind an ask-user card and a selected weekday.

red.purpose: Interrupt and destroy. Never used for 'important'.

code-keyword.purpose: Syntax keeps its own palette; driving it from the accent puts 'this commits' on every let.

focus-ring.purpose: Semi-transparent, so what is gated is the composite over the surface behind it (WCAG 1.4.11, 3:1).

edge.purpose: The structural frame, and only four jobs: a column's outer boundary, a header bar's underside, a footer bar's top, and the separator between rows of one list.

selection.purpose: ::selection, SEMI-TRANSPARENT and with no color override, so selected text keeps its own ink - syntax highlighting and inline-code chips survive being selected. Gated on the composite, never the declared colour. GitHub's dark theme does the same at #3392FF44.

code-fill.purpose: A token inside running text: inline code, a kbd hint. Louder than the interaction fill on purpose - a hover fill has the pointer to help it read, a code span has nothing.

page-title.purpose: The h1 of a pane: session title, settings page, agents, routines.

section-title.purpose: A block heading, one level down from the pane.

item-title.purpose: The name of one row. The READING face — a name is not a machine string.

body.purpose: Agent prose. Rhythm is tighter than a web article's: a transcript is scanned, not settled into.

legend.purpose: A small label. Sentence case, no tracking — the counterpart to the tightened titles.

readout.purpose: A live measured value. Tabular so digits never jitter as they tick.

code.purpose: Identifiers, paths, code blocks, tool output.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: The ONLY shadow in the system. Spent on things that genuinely float: menus, popovers, dialogs, and the two mobile overlays. Nothing else has elevation.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: A transcript turn arriving: opacity 0 to 1, translateY(3px) to 0. Class .animate-settle.

motion.name: latch
motion.purpose: A readout changing: opacity 0.25 to 1, re-keyed on the value. Class .animate-latch.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: The streaming cursor: a 0.12em bar in legend-dim, stepping between opacity 1 and 0.15.

motion.name: lamp-ping
motion.purpose: A lamp reporting live work: a ring scaling to 2.1 and fading. Class .lamp-live.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Collapses every animation and transition in the build to 0.01ms.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Transcript gutter goes inline below this.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Session rail becomes a drawer and the settings nav becomes a scrolling strip below this.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Task panel overlays the transcript and starts collapsed below this.

containers.name: transcript
containers.purpose: Transcript, composer, config bar, progression rows.

containers.name: prose
containers.purpose: Running text inside a reply, and only running text. Tables and code keep the full column.

containers.name: settings-nav
containers.purpose: The settings/admin nav column at md and up.

containers.name: task-panel
containers.purpose: The agent task list column at lg and up.

containers.name: header
containers.purpose: The one height every column header reads, so the app lines up across its seams.

accessibility.floor: WCAG AA 4.5:1 for every ink against all four surfaces (chassis, panel, panel-raised, screen) in both exposures, and WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 for the focus ring composited over each.
accessibility.interactionFill: panel-raised separates from panel by >=1.20 in all eight palettes; accent-quiet separates from panel-raised by >=1.10; edge separates from both chassis and panel by >=1.15; ::selection by >=1.20 from every surface it can land on. All floored by the gate. Inline code separates from the panel by >=1.35, since nothing points at it. Inline code separates from the panel by >=1.35, since nothing points at it.
accessibility.note: The gate DISCOVERS the worlds by scanning skins.css for data-skin blocks rather than carrying a list, and it parses the shipped CSS rather than restating values.
accessibility.selection: Wash visibility floored at 1.30 (measures 1.41-1.77); primary ink holds full AA over it (7.3-9.7); secondary ink floored at 4.3 WHILE SELECTED (5.9-6.9 at rest) - a measured trade, since holding every ink at 4.5 drops the wash to ~1.25. GitHub's dark theme measures ~1.42 visibility and ~4.44 muted text.

skins.note: Four worlds over identical layouts. A world replaces material, never structure: same components, same data-testids, same positions. Graphite is the default and carries no attribute, so index.css keeps the specificity it was written against. Ink/Aurora/Glass live in src/skins.css and each declares its FULL palette per exposure rather than patching Graphite. The seam defaults sit in @layer base because @import must come first, which would otherwise hand every seam value back to the default on source order alone.

worlds.name: Graphite
worlds.character: Cool graphite, the reference world. Enough colour to have an identity, quiet enough to watch for an hour.

worlds.name: Ink
worlds.character: Bright minimal, true neutral. The control that commits is the highest-contrast object on screen rather than the most colourful.

worlds.name: Aurora
worlds.character: Every ground carries the accent's own hue at low chroma, so the world reads as one colour rather than grey with a highlight stuck on it.

worlds.name: Glass
worlds.character: A tinted ground with two coloured lights on it, and the interface as a frosted sheet laid over the top. Regions separate by how much of the ground shows through.

components.name: Key
components.description: The default control: a filled rectangle with a word on it. No travel, no moulded edge, no engraved legend.

components.name: Field
components.description: A filled slot, not an outlined box. The fill is what says 'you can type here'; a border would say it a second time. Focus adds the accent ring.

components.name: Row
components.description: A list entry: padding and a hover fill. Not a card - a fill, a ring, a gap and a radius is four separations for one boundary.
variants: data-active / aria-selected carry the selection fill

components.name: Section
components.description: A region grouping content on the page. No fill, no line; whitespace and a title do the separating. Replaced .panel p-4 on every settings page.

components.name: Panel
components.description: A contained region with a fill and a radius, no border.

components.name: Floating
components.description: A menu, popover or dialog. The only place --float is spent.

components.name: Screen
components.description: Machine output: tool results, code blocks, log tails.

components.name: Lamp
components.description: A 7px status indicator, always paired with a word. Never colour alone.

components.name: Chip
components.description: A small filled tag, no border.

components.name: Readout
components.description: A live measured value, tabular so digits never jitter as they tick.

components.name: Titles
components.description: Three roles, one rendition each, so the same job never ships in two looks. All carry negative tracking; .legend, the label role, carries none.

components.name: Roster row
components.description: One entry in a roster - agents, environments, routines, workflows. A component rather than a pattern because the four pages had drifted into four dialects: mono names on two, three different delete controls at three icon sizes, two alignments.

narrative.overview: horsie is a long-running process you watch. The interface's whole job is to show its state and then get out of the way, so it is built as a single quiet surface rather than a stack of boxes. There is no chassis, no bezel and no card: a session, a settings page and a roster are all the same sheet, and what separates their regions is a small step in value, whitespace, and type weight.
keyCharacteristics: A line marks the chrome, never a region: column edges, header undersides, footer tops, list separators. Inside the frame, regions separate by value, whitespace and type weight.
A fill means something happened. Hover is the neutral fill; selected is the accent wash - two different jobs, two different fills.
One accent for the control that commits; live for a value in flight; red for interrupt and destroy; green for a healthy channel.
Two self-hosted faces: Inter for everything read, Geist Mono for identifiers, paths and code. No font ever comes from a CDN.
Titles carry negative tracking, labels carry none. Sentence case throughout.
The density is deliberately tight - this is a transcript you scan, not an essay you settle into.
A status is always a lamp AND a word.
Light and dark are the same design at two exposures, not two designs.
Every ink clears WCAG AA against every surface it can land on, in all four worlds and both exposures - measured, not assumed.
rules: The frame holds the layout together; without column edges and bar edges the columns float and the app stops reading as one instrument.
Inside the frame, if a region needs bounding it needs space - not a border.
Hover and selection must be different fills, or neither reads.
One focus indicator, not two: the ring alone. A solid accent border AND a 3px halo is 4px of heavy colour round every input.
A region painted for no reason costs the fills that do mean something.
The rails are chassis and the content is panel, in that order. Painting the rail lighter than the content inverts the reading.
panel-raised is the interaction fill, so its brightness flips between exposures. Holding material roles by brightness in both is what made every light-mode hover invisible.
One accent, spent only on the control that commits. A fifth colour would have to displace one of the four.
Syntax highlighting keeps its own code-* palette.
A name is not a machine string: .item-title is the reading face, and font-mono is for paths, ids, aliases and code.
One shadow, spent only on things that genuinely float. Modelling depth on a surface that has none is what produced the boxes.
Anything a world must vary needs a new seam variable, never a call-site override.
Every column header reads --header-h, so the app lines up across its seams without any of them agreeing on a number separately.
AA is measured by contrast.mjs against the shipped CSS, and the gate discovers the worlds rather than listing them.
Inline code gets its own fill, not the interaction fill: a hover fill is sized to be a whisper because the pointer helps it read, and a code span has no pointer.
::selection is a transparent wash with no color override, so syntax highlighting and code chips survive selection. Gate the composite, not the declared colour.
Inline code gets its own fill, not the interaction fill: a hover fill is sized to be a whisper because the pointer helps it read, and a code span has no pointer.
dos: Draw the frame with the *-edge-* utilities: column-edge-r/l, bar-edge-b/t, list-divided.
Use panel-raised for hover and accent-quiet for selected.
Spend a fill on hover, selection, or machine output.
Add a seam variable when a world needs to vary something.
Use .section for a group of content on a page, .panel for a contained surface, .floating for a menu or dialog.
Use .row for a list entry: padding and a hover fill.
Use .item-title for the name of a row, in the reading face.
Pair every status colour with a word.
Run bun run contrast after any token change.
donts: Do not reach for a border inside the frame.
Do not use the same fill for hover and selection.
Do not paint a region just to show it is a region.
Do not override a seam value at a call site.
Do not build a card per row - a fill, a ring, a gap and a radius is four separations for one boundary.
Do not reach for font-mono unless the string is genuinely a machine string.
Do not add a second shadow or an elevation scale.
Do not signal state with colour alone, in any world.
Do not lower a contrast threshold to make the gate pass.
Do not give ::selection a solid background or a color override.

components_note: Each entry points at the class it names. The CSS of record is clients/web/src/index.css - restating it here gives it a second copy free to drift.
